title: Update on crypto bot: Shifted from 15m noise to 30m/1h rule centroids & multi-strategy ensemble (Feedback appreciated)
author: Trader_for_earner
selftext:
Hey everyone,

Thanks a lot for the feedback on my last post regarding chop regimes, TTL decay exits, and the curve-fitting warnings.

Based on the suggestions, I ran a systematic quantitative overhaul across 5 crypto perpetuals (FIL, WLD, NEAR, APT, ADA) using Walk-Forward Optimization (WFO) with Permutation Noise stress-testing.

Here is what changed and what the data showed:

TIMEFRAME RESOLUTION: LEAVING THE "15M GAMBLE"

5m / 15m: Failed Walk-Forward Out-Of-Sample validation (Profit Factor 0.57 - 0.75). As someone rightly pointed out in the last thread, running pure momentum on 15m is a noise trap unless you sit out 80% of sessions.

30m / 1h: Survived with an Out-Of-Sample Profit Factor of 1.74 across 92 trades and a 100% WFO window pass rate. Market maker liquidity sweeps got absorbed into candle bodies on 30m/1h.

FROM TUNING SL/TP WRAPPERS TO "INTERNAL RULE CENTROIDS"

Instead of just adjusting external stop-loss and take-profit multipliers, we exposed and tuned the internal algorithmic knobs for 4 distinct expansion setups:

A. IMPULSE\_EXPANSION:

Net Displacement: tested 1.2x to 2.0x ATR -> Centroid: 1.4x ATR

Volume Multiplier: tested 1.0x to 2.2x SMA20 -> Centroid: 1.5x SMA

Candle Body Dominance: tested 40% to 60% -> Centroid: 50% solid body

Composite Conviction Score Cutoff: Centroid: 0.60

B. KELTNER\_SQUEEZE:

Compression Duration: Centroid: >= 3 bars (Bollinger inside Keltner)

Breakout ADX Hurdle: Centroid: >= 18

C. BREAKOUT\_RETEST:

Swing Lookback: 30 bars | Rejection Wick: 40%

D. TREND\_PULLBACK:

HTF Filter: EMA 50/200 | Pullback Depth: 0.8x ATR

Rather than picking the single highest curve-fitted PnL combination, we clustered all parameter sets that were profitable across multiple Out-Of-Sample windows and calculated the geometric centroid (median) of the plateau.

THE WIN RATE VS. PAYOFF TRADE-OFF

Execution Geometry: Centroid settled on SL: 1.8x ATR and TP: 1.8x Risk (1:1.80 Risk/Reward).

The Metric Shift: Because our target is asymmetric (1.8R), our realized Win Rate dropped from scalping levels down to around 41.2%.

However, because the payoff ratio is 1.80, the system delivers an overall Profit Factor of 1.67 - 1.74 with a maximum consecutive losing streak of 4 trades.

PER-COIN & REGIME ATTRIBUTION (NOT JUST POOLED DATA)

Looking into the individual coin matrices:

FILUSDT: Thrives in IMPULSE\_EXPANSION (PF 1.86, all regimes) and BREAKOUT\_RETEST in weak trends (PF 6.94).

WLDUSDT: Thrives in KELTNER\_SQUEEZE (PF 1.97).

NEARUSDT: Thrives in TREND\_PULLBACK and high-volatility expansions (PF 17.90).

APTUSDT & ADAUSDT: Marginal performers across universal rules; need to sit out high-chop regimes entirely.

QUESTIONS FOR THE COMMUNITY:

Centroid vs. Bayesian: For those running production crypto algos, how do you handle parameter stability across regime shifts? Do you prefer cluster/centroid medians over Bayesian optimization?

Exits in Low-Vol Regimes: During extended BTC compression (like the recent 83k-87k chop where trades stall at +1.2R before reaching 1.8R), do you recommend keeping the fixed 1.8R target to avoid curve-fitting future breakouts, or do you dynamically scale targets down to 1.1R based on ATR/regime?

Win Rate Acceptance: For systematic trend/expansion traders, is a \~40% Win Rate with 1.8R standard in your books, or do you gate more aggressively (e.g. higher volume hurdles) to push Win Rate above 50% at the expense of trade frequency?

Appreciate any insights or critiques on the architecture!

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Moving from tuning wrappers to a plateau centroid is a good step. A few things I'd look at: 92 out-of-sample trades across five coins is a small sample, and per-coin or per-regime profit factors like 6.94 and 17.90 almost certainly rest on a handful of trades, so I'd show the trade count beside each. Count every parameter combination and setup you screened toward the trial total, and keep the exit fixed at 1.8R and compare it with the 1.1R version on the same trades before deciding. A 40% win rate with 1.8R is normal, and a higher win rate is only an improvement if expectancy per trade holds. Scheduled macro days often explain the stalls and sudden expansions, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for splitting results by them.
